pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word in The teacher counted the votes is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. counted
   B. the
   C. votes
   D. teacher

2. Why should a writer plan a story before writing? (1 mark)
   A. To skip the ending
   B. To lose the ideas
   C. To avoid a title
   D. To organise the ideas

3. Why is it important to obey leaders? (1 mark)
   A. It is a game
   B. It is boring
   C. It makes noise
   D. It keeps order, peace and safety

4. What should you do in a reading competition? (1 mark)
   A. Read very fast
   B. Read clearly with the right intonation
   C. Shout
   D. Whisper

5. What is a tongue twister? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of drum
   B. A silent poem
   C. A phrase that is hard to say fast
   D. A very long word

6. In a singing game, who gives the instructions? (1 mark)
   A. The oldest pupil always
   B. Nobody
   C. The soloist
   D. The audience only

7. What is a customer? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of shop
   B. A type of money
   C. A person who buys
   D. A person who sells only

8. Where should letters sit in a lined book? (1 mark)
   A. Above the page
   B. Outside the margin
   C. On the base line
   D. Under the desk

9. What is the plural of the English word loaf? (1 mark)
   A. loaves
   B. loafs
   C. loafes
   D. loaf

10. Which question word asks for a reason? (1 mark)
   A. Where
   B. When
   C. Why
   D. Who

11. In Simon says, when should you obey an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Only if you like it
   B. Only when it begins with Simon says
   C. Never
   D. Always

12. What does pronunciation mean? (1 mark)
   A. The way we say the sounds of words
   B. The meaning of a word
   C. The length of a story
   D. The way we write words

13. What is a word puzzle used for? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking
   B. Running
   C. Painting
   D. Practising vocabulary in a fun way

14. Which word in an advert may be used to persuade? (1 mark)
   A. paper
   B. door
   C. best
   D. table

15. Which is a good ending for a story? (1 mark)
   A. It has no meaning
   B. It repeats the title
   C. It begins a new topic
   D. It solves the problem or shows the lesson

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Name three ways to practise letter shapes before writing them. (3 marks)

17. Describe what an imaginative composition is. (2 marks)

18. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)

19. After listening to a safety story, describe how you would answer four kinds of comprehension questions and give one example of each. (5 marks)

20. List three note points from a passage about a kite on a free day. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — counted
   Counted shows the action.

2. D — To organise the ideas
   A plan gives the story shape.

3. D — It keeps order, peace and safety
   Obeying fair leaders keeps everyone safe.

4. B — Read clearly with the right intonation
   Clear reading with expression is judged.

5. C — A phrase that is hard to say fast
   Tongue twisters train clear speech.

6. C — The soloist
   The soloist leads by singing the instructions and the group responds.

7. C — A person who buys
   A customer buys goods or services.

8. C — On the base line
   Letters rest on the base line.

9. A — loaves
   Loaf changes f to ves in the plural.

10. C — Why
   Why asks the reason.

11. B — Only when it begins with Simon says
   The game is about listening carefully.

12. A — The way we say the sounds of words
   Pronunciation is how words are said.

13. D — Practising vocabulary in a fun way
   Puzzles help pupils remember words.

14. C — best
   Words such as best persuade people to buy.

15. D — It solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trace in the air, trace on a card, model with clay or string, paint them.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: A story that comes from the writer's imagination and is not a true report.
   Working / marking points: One mark for story and one for imagination.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is quick reading for the main idea and scanning is quick searching for a specific fact.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition.

19. (5 marks)
   Answer: Answer who with a person (his mother), what with an event (touched the pot), where with a place (the clinic) and why with a reason (he wanted to see the steam). Give short, full answers and ask for repetition if needed.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each kind and example, and one mark for full sentences.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: Children go to the field, fly a paper kite, string breaks, grandfather mends the kite (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each short correct note.
